_doc: ARTICLE SOURCES — lets the user switch where article/timeline/tone data comes from: the self-hosted GDELT proxy (data/topics.json's `api.base`), the self-hosted ntfy/rss-gateway mesh feed, or a well-known public RSS/Atom feed fetched directly from the handset. Adding a source is an entry HERE plus a rebuild — no Kotlin change, same pattern as data/topics.json. Baked into BuildConfig.SOURCES_B64 by app/build.gradle. Every url below was probed and item-counted by hand before being added; none are placeholders or guesses — do not add a source (or a channel) without doing the same. EVERY source now exposes SUB-CHANNELS (see `channels` below) so the UI can show a two-row nav: row 1 picks the source, row 2 picks the channel within it.
_doc_fields: id: stable key, used as the persisted 'active source' value and (for a non-query-driven rss source with no explicit channel picked yet) as the fallback synthetic channel id. label: shown in the UI source picker. kind: 'gdelt' (talks to api.base from topics.json, one query per topic) or 'rss' (parses an RSS2.0/RSS1.0(RDF)/Atom feed directly). url: rss only, and only meaningful for a QUERY-DRIVEN feed — the feed URL with a literal '{query}' placeholder substituted (URL-encoded) per topic; a fixed rss source's articles come from its `channels[].url` instead, never from this top-level `url`. query_driven: true if the source takes a search term per topic (gdelt-self, google-news) — for these, `channels` is INTENTIONALLY OMITTED here and synthesized at runtime 1:1 from the user's topics store (NewsBridge), so adding a topic in the Topics tab shows up as a channel with no duplication of the topic list into this file; false if it's one or more fixed feeds regardless of topic. channels: declared sub-feeds for a fixed rss source — `[{id, label, url}]`, each fetched only when it is the ACTIVE channel (never all of a source's channels on one refresh — that would be N× pointless traffic against feeds the user isn't even looking at). dynamic_channels: true only for ntfy-self — its channels are NOT declared here at all (there are ~142 of them and they change as the user's self-hosted infrastructure changes); they're discovered at runtime from `channels_url`, cached on disk, and re-discovered on every sync — see NewsModels.kt's DynamicChannels and NewsSync.kt's syncRssDynamic. base/channels_url: dynamic_channels only — `base` is prefixed onto a discovered channel's id when the discovery payload omits an explicit feed url; `channels_url` is the JSON endpoint listing the channels themselves. capabilities: subset of ['articles','timeline','tone'] this source can actually produce — no RSS source below carries a tone/sentiment field, so every rss entry lists only 'articles'; a UI must not offer timeline/tone charts for a source that doesn't declare that capability. requires_mesh: true for gdelt-self and ntfy-self, both of which need the self-hosted proxy/mesh (public gateway or WireGuard mesh) to be reachable; every other rss source is fetched straight from the public internet.

sources.label: Cloud Feeds (ntfy)
sources._doc_source: ea_cloud-superapp/data/cloud_services.json (service `ntfy`, vm oci-A1-f_0, port 8090, public_url https://rss.diegonmarcos.com) + ea_cloud-superapp/data/services_private.json (`rss-gateway`, private_dns rss-gateway:8091) + ea_cloud-mail/build.json's COMMS_RSS_BASE + ea_cloud-mail/patches/0055-...: rss-gateway serves /feed/channels.json (142 channels: 22 declared + 89 logs + 31 apps) on wg0, feed_auth=none. Channels are deliberately NOT enumerated here — see the top-level _doc_fields entry for dynamic_channels.
